nodes.label: Vizuální principy
nodes.community_name: KENJI KNIHOVNA — Kontext projektu pro Claude Code

nodes.label: Explicit authorization for external changes
nodes.rationale: Git push, production deploys, Ecomail sends, and production service mutations require Daniel's explicit instruction.

nodes.label: Monthly batched production release
nodes.rationale: Production changes are accumulated for at most one explicitly initiated deployment per calendar month to reduce Netlify credit consumption and preserve review time.

nodes.label: Global AI usage limit
nodes.rationale: A service-role-only database counter limits anonymous AI usage and protects inference costs.

nodes.label: Soft JavaScript paywall
nodes.rationale: The MVP hides premium content in JavaScript; truly preventing download would require a server-rendered implementation.

nodes.label: People, tools, content, coupons, emailing and activity modules
nodes.norm_label: people, tools, content, coupons, emailing and activity modules

nodes.label: Free, Databáze and Academy access tiers
nodes.norm_label: free, databaze and academy access tiers

nodes.label: Audience-first campaign sequencing
nodes.rationale: The exact safe recipient audience must be audited and tagged before copy approval, template creation, testing, or campaign launch.

nodes.label: One campaign per segment
nodes.rationale: Ecomail sends a campaign configured with multiple segments only to the first segment, so each campaign must target exactly one segment.

nodes.label: Transactional and marketing email split
nodes.rationale: Resend is reserved for authentication and purchase messages while Ecomail owns marketing sequences and newsletters.

nodes.label: Shared asset cache versioning
nodes.rationale: Explicit and consistent asset versions prevent browsers from retaining stale shared CSS or JavaScript after changes.

nodes.label: Value-first onboarding
nodes.rationale: Free users should receive immediate practical value, a reason to return, and a natural view of the paid product's value.

nodes.label: Verified identity security model
nodes.rationale: Admin access, community publishing, and user-scoped operations derive identity from a signed Supabase JWT rather than trusting browser-provided email.

nodes.label: Server-side Stripe Checkout
nodes.rationale: Stripe secret keys remain in Netlify Functions, and successful checkout webhooks update the user's Supabase tier.

nodes.label: OTP template selection for new users
nodes.norm_label: otp template selection for new users
nodes.rationale: Supabase signInWithOtp uses Confirm sign up for a new address and Magic link for an existing member, so both templates must be maintained.

nodes.label: Security-definer lead and progress RPC
nodes.rationale: Anonymous clients can register leads and save progress through narrow RPC functions while RLS prevents downloading the users table.
